reasons: All 19 nodes pass against the implementation and the recipe demonstrably fails without it (first behavioural assertion times out), so it is a real validator rather than a rubber stamp.
Every acceptance criterion is proved by a state assertion, and the three copy variants are additionally shown in stitched screenshots with the HUD suppressed, so the claim is provable both ways.
Both the positive and negative sides of the behaviour are asserted: the warning must appear for a crossing ladder and must clear itself on a side flip without any endpoint edit.
better_version_guidance: Assert the submit-time re-validation path directly. AC 4's submit half currently only emits a DevLogger line; a watch_logs node reading from a captured baseline offset would turn that into proof instead of inference.
Drive the endpoint values from the live top-of-book instead of hardcoding prices around BTC's current level, so the recipe does not silently degrade if BTC moves far from ~77k.

coverage.reason: All five acceptance criteria have at least one dedicated assertion node; AC 4 is covered on both the endpoint-edit and side-flip axes.

graph_quality.reason: Linear graph with an explicit direction reset after navigation, so the run does not inherit leftover form state from a previous run. That defect was caught and fixed during authoring.

evidence_fit.reason: Mixed proof: assertions for every claim plus a screenshot per copy variant. Capturing the frames exposed two recipe defects (incomplete ticket, mis-ordered ladder) that the assertions alone had missed.

flake_risk.reason: Endpoint prices are hardcoded around BTC ~77k. A large move would put the chosen values on the wrong side of the book and flip assertions. Acceptable for a branch gate; would need live-price parameterisation for CI.

failing_first.reason: Verified by stashing the implementation, restarting the app onto that source, and re-running: fail at expect-partial-above with present=false.

contextual_findings.message: The submit-time re-validation in onPlaceOrderPress is exercised only indirectly. It emits a DevLogger line rather than changing visible state, so the recipe does not assert on it; the unit tests cover the helper it calls.
expect-quiet passes in both worlds because the message element is absent with and without the feature. Retained deliberately as a guard against over-warning, not counted as feature proof.

A ui.wait_for on the warning passes even when a blocking validation error occupies the same slot or Place order is disabled. Two such defects survived a fully green run and were only caught once the frames were inspected.

suggested_recipe_delta: Add a watch_logs node, offset from a pre-run baseline line count, asserting the submit-time crossing marker fires when the order is placed while crossing.
Read the live best bid/ask into params and derive the endpoint values from it instead of hardcoding prices near 77k.

anti_patterns: Concluding a UI claim is unprovable visually because the element renders below the fold. --hud hide plus ui.capture_surface solve both the overlay and the clipping; anchoring the scroll on the element above the target keeps it in frame.
Authoring a multi-node recipe blind: the first full run failed at expect-quiet purely because the form kept the Short side from an earlier probe. An explicit direction-reset node was the fix.
Trusting a green ui.wait_for as proof the user would see the message: it passes even when a blocking error occupies the same slot or the submit button is disabled.
good_patterns: Validating each node standalone via mm-harness call before appending it to the recipe.
Proving failing-first by stashing the implementation and restarting the app, rather than asserting it from reasoning.
Inspecting every captured frame rather than trusting the run's exit code — the screenshots found two recipe defects that a fully green run had hidden.
